Alle Frauen verlassen in grösster Bestür: All the women leave the hall in the greatest dismay and with gestures of horror. Elisabeth, who had listened to the contest of the minstrels with growing anxiety, remains behind alone among the women—pale, supporting herself upright by one of the wooden pillars of the canopy only with the greatest exertion of her strength.—The Landgrave, all the knights, and minstrels have left their seats and assemble together.—Tannhäuser, on the extreme left, remains for some time as if in ecstasy.
Alle dringen mit gezücktem Schwerte auf: All press forward toward Tannhäuser with drawn swords; he assumes a defiant posture; Elisabeth rushes between them.
Alle haben unwillkürlich ihre Gebärden g: All have involuntarily moderated their gestures; Elisabeth, as if to protect Tannhäuser once more, had placed herself in front of those pressing forward anew; she now points to the promise-filled song of the young pilgrims.—Tannhäuser suddenly pauses in the midst of the most passionate contrition and listens to the song.
Alle halten in grösster Betroffenheit an: All pause in the greatest consternation.
Alle setzen sich Die vier Edelknaben tre: All sit down. The four pages step forward; they collect in a golden cup the name of each minstrel written on a rolled-up slip of paper;—then they present the cup to Elisabeth, who draws out one of the slips and hands it back to the pages; they read the name and then solemnly step into the center.
Allgemeines Erstaunen. Elisabeth im Wide: General astonishment. Elisabeth torn between enraptured fascination and anxious bewilderment. Biterolf rises quickly and angrily.
Gradually this image also fades. The fragrant mist finally disperses completely, revealing the entire grotto solitary and still. The Graces bow playfully before Venus and slowly withdraw toward the grotto of love. Deepest tranquility. Unchanged group of Venus and Tannhäuser.
Als er tiefer in das Tal hinabsteigen wi: As he is about to descend deeper into the valley, he hears the song of the pilgrims and stops.
Das ganze Tal wimmelt jetzt vom immer no: The whole valley now teems with the ever-growing hunting party. The Landgrave and the minstrels turn to the hunters; the Landgrave blows his horn; loud blaring of horns and barking of hounds answer him. While the Landgrave and the minstrels mount the horses brought to them from the Wartburg, the curtain falls.
Der Gesang verhallt allmählich; die Sonn: The singing gradually dies away; the sun sets.
Der Hirt, den Gesang vernehmend, hält au: The shepherd, hearing the song, pauses on his shawm and listens devoutly.
Der Landgraf tritt aus einer Seitentüre: The Landgrave enters from a side door; Elisabeth hurries toward him and buries her face on his chest.
Der Landgraf tritt feierlich in die Mitt: The Landgrave solemnly steps into the center.
Der Landgraf und Elisabeth treten an den: The Landgrave and Elisabeth step onto the balcony to watch for the arrival of the guests. Four pages enter and announce them. They receive orders from the Landgrave for the reception, etc. (Trumpets in the castle courtyard) (From here on, the knights and counts enter individually with noble ladies and retinue, who remain in the background, and are received by the Landgrave and Elisabeth).
Der Zug der Pilger biegt von hier an auf: From here, the procession of pilgrims turns left onto the mountain path by the shrine of the Virgin Mary and thus leaves the stage;—the shepherd likewise departs with his shawm to the right from the height;—the herd bells are heard ever more in the distance.
Der rosige Duft schliesst sich wieder, d: The rosy mist closes again, the image disappears, and the Graces now signify the mysterious content of the picture as a work of love through a graceful dance. The mist parts once more. In gentle moonlight dusk, Leda is seen stretched out by the forest pond; the swan swims toward her and caressingly rests his neck upon her bosom.
Die Nebel beginnen in rosiger Dämmerung: The mists begin to glow in a rosy dusk.
Die Nebel verfinstern sich allmählich; h: The mists gradually darken; bright torchlight then flares up through them.
Die Pilger haben hier die Bühne bereits: The pilgrims have already left the stage here.
Die Pilger haben sich hier bereits der H: The pilgrims have already turned toward the background here, gradually moving into the distance.
Die Sängerhalle auf der Wartburg; im Hin: The Minstrels' Hall at the Wartburg Castle; in the background, an open view of the courtyard and the valley.
Die Versammelten haben alle die ihnen an: The assembled company have all taken the seats assigned to them, forming a large semicircle. The Landgrave and Elisabeth occupy seats of honor in the foreground under a canopy. (Trumpets on stage) The minstrels enter and bow solemnly with knightly greeting to the assembly; then they take the seats designated for them in a smaller semicircle in the vacant center of the hall, Tannhäuser in the middle ground on the right, Wolfram at the opposite end on the left, facing the assembly. The Landgrave rises.
Ein jäher Hoffnungsstrahl leuchtet ihm,: A sudden ray of hope shines upon him; he throws himself with convulsive vehemence at Elisabeth's feet, fervently and hurriedly kisses the hem of her robe, and then breaks out, reeling with immense agitation, with the cry:
Elisabeth drückt ihm abermals durch Gebä: Elisabeth expresses to him once more through gestures that she thanks him and his faithful love with all her heart; but that her path leads her toward heaven, where she has a high office to fulfill; he should therefore let her go unaccompanied and not follow her. She ascends halfway up the mountain and gradually disappears along the footpath leading towards the Wartburg, after her figure has long been seen in the distance. Wolfram, who has long followed Elisabeth with his eyes, sits down at the foot of the hill to the left of the valley and begins to play upon the harp.
Er bleibt an die Mauerbrüstung gelehnt i: He remains leaning against the stone parapet in the background.
Er setzt sich erschöpft auf Fusse des Be: He sits down exhausted at the foot of the mountain ledge; Wolfram is about to sit down by his side as well.
Er stirbt. - Alle senken die Fackeln zur: He dies.—All lower their torches to the earth and extinguish them. Morning dawn fully illuminates the scene.
Er verbleibt mit gen Himmel gerichtetem: He remains continuing to play the harp with his eyes directed toward heaven.
Es ist gänzlich Nacht geworden. Tannhäus: It has become completely night. Tannhäuser enters; he wears torn pilgrim's garments, his countenance is pale and disfigured; he totters with weary steps, leaning upon his staff.
Finstere Nacht; leichte Nebel verhüllen: Dark night; light mists gradually veil the scene.
Hier betreten die Pilger die Bühne von r: Here the pilgrims enter the stage from the right in the foreground.
Hier betritt der Zug die Bühne in der Ti: Here the procession enters the stage in the depths of the valley, the older pilgrims leading—the minstrels closest to the open coffin in which Elisabeth's body is carried by them; the Landgrave, knights, and nobles follow the coffin.
Hier macht Wolfram eine Gebärde, welche: Here Wolfram makes a gesture that prompts the minstrels, as they recognize Tannhäuser, to set down the coffin.
In einer hellen, rosigen Beleuchtung ers: In a bright, rosy light Venus appears, resting upon her couch.
Indem sie ihn sanft nach sich zu ziehen: While gently seeking to draw him toward herself.
Man hört den Gesang der älteren Pilger,: The singing of the older pilgrims is heard approaching along the mountain path from the direction of the Wartburg. The shepherd plays on his shawm.
Sie dringen von neuem auf Tannhäuser ein: They press forward anew toward Tannhäuser.
Sie führt die Hand sanft über seine Stir: She gently passes her hand across his forehead.
Sie macht eine Bewegung, sich zu entfern: She makes a movement to depart.
Sie nimmt die Harfe und hält sie ihm vor: She takes the harp and holds it before him.
Sie setzen sich zu Füssen des Landgrafen: They sit down at the feet of the Landgrave and Elisabeth. Wolfram rises. Tannhäuser leans upon his harp, as if falling into a reverie.
Sie verbleibt eine Zeitlang wie in andäc: She remains for some time as if in devout rapt contemplation; as she then slowly rises, she catches sight of Wolfram, who approaches to address her. She begs him with a gesture not to speak to her.
Sie versinkt. Die Nebel verschwinden gän: She sinks. The mists disappear completely. Morning dawn.—From the Wartburg a funeral procession with torches descends toward the depths of the valley.
Sie ziehen während des Folgenden an dem: During what follows, they pass by the mountain ledge, slowly proceeding along the valley toward the background.
Tannhäuser betrachtet Wolfram lange mit: Tannhäuser gazes at Wolfram for a long time in touched astonishment.
Tannhäuser fährt wie aus dem Traume auf;: Tannhäuser starts up as if from a dream; his defiant expression instantly turns into one of rapturous ecstasy with which he stares into the air before him; a slight trembling of the hand unconsciously reaching for the harp strings, and an uncanny smile upon his lips reveal that an alien enchantment has taken possession of him. When he then, as if awakening, strikes the harp vigorously, his whole demeanor shows that he scarcely knows where he is any longer, and in particular takes no more notice of Elisabeth.
Tannhäuser in der Weg tretend, mit erhob: Stepping into Tannhäuser's path, with raised voice.
Tannhäuser ist von Wolfram zum Sarge gel: Tannhäuser has been led by Wolfram to the coffin; bending over Elisabeth's body, he slowly sinks down.
Tannhäuser trennt sich von Elisabeth; er: Tannhäuser parts from Elisabeth; he approaches Wolfram, embraces him warmly, and departs with him by the stairs. Elisabeth gazes after Tannhäuser from the balcony.
Tannhäuser zuckt mit dem Haupte empor, a: Tannhäuser raises his head with a start, as if waking from a dream.—Venus draws him back caressingly. Tannhäuser passes his hand over his eyes, as if trying to hold fast to a dream image.
Tannhäuser, der in der Mitte der Bühne w: Tannhäuser, who had stood rooted to the center of the stage, sinks violently shaken to his knees.
Tannhäuser, der überrascht und schnell a: Tannhäuser, who had started up quickly in surprise, collects himself and bows silently to the Landgrave after casting a fleeting glance at him and the minstrels.
Tannhäuser, von Wolfram geleitet, tritt: Tannhäuser, led by Wolfram, enters with him from the stairs in the background.
Tannhäuser, von heftiger Rührung ergriff: Tannhäuser, seized by profound emotion, rushes into Wolfram's arms, warmly greets each of the minstrels in turn, and bows with heartfelt gratitude before the Landgrave.
Trompeten im Hintergrunde tief, wie im B: Trumpets deep in the background, as if in the castle courtyard.
Tränen ersticken seine Stimme; er neigt: Tears choke his voice; he bows his head deep to the earth and seems lost in grief; from the direction of Eisenach, ringing of bells is heard.
Venus hat sich mit einem Schrei abgewand: Venus has turned away with a cry, hiding her face in her hands.—Long silence. Then she gradually seeks Tannhäuser's gaze again, turning to him suddenly with an alluring smile. At her signal, an enchanted grotto appears, to which she points.
Waldhörner entfernt. Während sich der Kl: Hunting horns in the distance. As the sound of the horns gradually draws near, the distant chiming of bells falls silent. Down from the hill on the left, from a forest path, the Landgrave and the minstrels enter individually in hunting attire.
Wirre Bewegungen tanzender Gestalten wer: Confused movements of dancing figures become visible.
Wolfram bleibt in geringer Entfernung vo: Wolfram stops a short distance in front of Tannhäuser.
Während des Vorhergehenden hat sich nach: During what precedes, the Landgrave's entire hunting party, with falconers etc., has gathered on stage. The hunters blow their horns.
